# MyOS Customer Payment Instruction

A standalone or embedded Payment Instruction that adds correlated customer-session preparation and a guarantor-authorized payment attempt. Session readiness does not establish authorization, secured funds or payment completion. The inherited Payment Instruction protocol handles financial requests and guarantor outcome reports.

## Configuration and state

All paths belong to the instruction’s own document, including when embedded.

- `/paymentDetails/customerPaymentTerms/provider` identifies the provider, and `recipientPaymentAccountId` in the same object identifies the recipient payment account. Preparation requires both to be nonempty text.
- `paymentWindowDays` in that object defaults during preparation to `30` when omitted. It must be an integer from `1` through `3650`. It determines the payment deadline relative to the preparation execution timestamp, using a microsecond time scale.
- `/paymentTerms/amountMinor` supplies the full amount for the customer’s `secure` request; the operation does not accept an amount or recipient override. The currency source is not specified in the supplied definitions.
- `/paymentTerms/payerChannel` identifies the party named in the payment action description.

The included `clauses.customerSessionState` has a `state` pointer binding defaulting to `/customerSession`. Its initial `status` is `idle`; `requestId`, `id`, `paymentAttemptId` and `failureReason` are empty strings; `paymentDueAt` and `expiresAt` are `0`. These are initialization values, not substitutes for absent document data. Missing state remains unknown.

`requestId` correlates session preparation; `id` identifies the provider session; `paymentAttemptId` identifies the separate financial attempt. `paymentDueAt` is the instruction’s deadline, and `expiresAt` is the matching expiry reported for the provider session. `/payment/accepted` and `/payment/closed` belong to the inherited financial state.

## Session lifecycle

A `Payment Instruction Accepted` event triggers preparation. Preparation requires `/payment/accepted` to be `true`, validates the account configuration and payment window, then records `requestId: customer-session-1`, changes `status` to `requested`, and records `paymentDueAt`. Any status other than `idle` returns `duplicate`, so repeated acceptance does not restart preparation.

The following operations are bound to `guarantor`, invoke the inherited active-party check, and require an accepted instruction. The detailed active-party admission rules are not included here.

- **`provideSession`** requires a nonempty `requestId` matching the preparation request, a nonempty durable `sessionId`, and a positive integer `expiresAt` exactly equal to `paymentDueAt`. From `requested`, it stores the session ID and expiry, changes `status` to `ready`, and emits `Customer Payment Session Ready` with the correlated identifiers and expiry. An identical response while already `ready` is a duplicate; conflicting IDs or expiry are rejected. Other statuses are rejected. This operation does not check whether the deadline has already passed, so `ready` alone does not establish that a new attempt remains timely.
- **`failSessionPreparation`** requires the matching nonempty preparation `requestId` and a nonempty stable `reason`. From `requested`, it records `status: failed` and `failureReason`, and emits `Customer Payment Session Preparation Failed`. Repeating the same failure is a duplicate; changing its reason or reporting failure from another status is rejected. This represents a known terminal preparation failure. An unknown preparation outcome retains the pending request.
- **`requestCustomerPayment`** requires a nonempty financial `requestId` and a nonempty `sessionId` matching a `ready` session. A first attempt is rejected at or after `paymentDueAt`, or when `/payment/closed` is `true`. It delegates a `secure` request for `/paymentTerms/amountMinor` to the inherited payment protocol, records `paymentAttemptId`, and removes `/paymentAction`. Once an attempt ID is recorded, a different ID is rejected. Reusing the same ID delegates to inherited request handling before these new-attempt deadline and closed checks; the acceptance and matching-session checks still apply. Further financial guards and replay handling depend on the inherited functions.

When a session becomes ready, `/paymentAction` contains `kind: customer-payment`, the session identifier as `id`, the payer channel as `party`, and the preparation `requestId`. This is an action description with an opaque nonsecret ID. It grants no authority and establishes no personal obligation. Its removal when an attempt is recorded does not confirm payment success.

## Financial responses

Inherited operations remain on the `guarantor` channel. `acceptPaymentInstruction` accepts an empty request object with an optional text `reason`; `rejectPaymentInstruction` requires a nonempty `reason`.

Financial outcome reports correlate by a nonempty `requestId` to a recorded request in `payment.requests` or `payment.controlRequests`:

| Financial action | Success report | Declined report | Failed report | Unknown report |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secure funds | `secureFunds` | `declineSecureFunds` | `failSecureFunds` | `recordFundsSecuringUnknown` |
| Capture / complete | `completePayment` | `declineCompletePayment` | `failCompletePayment` | `recordPaymentCompletionUnknown` |
| Void before completion | `cancelBeforeCompletion` | `declineCancelBeforeCompletion` | `failCancelBeforeCompletion` | `recordPaymentCancellationUnknown` |
| Refund after completion | `reverseAfterCompletion` | `declineReverseAfterCompletion` | `failReverseAfterCompletion` | `recordPaymentReversalUnknown` |

Declined, failed and unknown reports require a nonempty `reason`. Optional `amount`, `amountMinor`, `amountSecured`, `amountCompleted` and `amountReversed` are assertions: each supplied value must equal the recorded request amount. They do not select a new amount. A requested amount, secured funds, completed payment and reversal remain distinct; an unknown report does not confirm success or terminal failure. Detailed balance updates and aggregate populations are not established by the supplied financial function bodies.

`recordTransactionInitiated` takes a nonempty `transactionId` containing neither `/` nor `~`. Optional `initiatedAmount` defaults during execution to `paymentTerms.amountMinor`; `attachmentPoint`, `providerReference` and `railType` are optional transaction details. `recordTransactionInitiationFailed` requires a correlated `requestId` and nonempty `reason`.

Inherited control responses also cover final-amount resolution, payee assignment, transaction-detail updates, and locking or unlocking completion, reversal and detail updates. They respond to recorded control requests; confirmation, rejection and failure are separate outcomes. Additional validation and ledger effects are delegated to inherited functions not shown here. An operation result of `acceptedNew` or `duplicate` describes handling of that operation, not a universal confirmation that money moved.

## Clause integration

The instruction inherits clause installation and amendment processing, with `partyRosterFrozen` set to `true`. Payment initialization is invoked after clause initialization or on `Document Activated` only while `/payment/accepted` is absent and either no activation clause exists or `/activation/active` is `true`.

Amendments carry `requestId`, `expectedRevision`, `expectedConfigurationId` and `changes`. Processing checks configuration freshness, clause keys, change targets and required clause configuration, then invokes exact clause-type configuration and transition hooks. A requested or prepared amendment is not proof of installation: `Amendment Accepted` denotes a fully installed material transition, while `Amendment Rejected` preserves effective configuration and state.
